sectionProgressions.description: Six-beat metric cycle (4 beats of heavy riff + 2 beats of resolving chord stabs)
Massive wall of overdriven guitars under Chris Cornell's soaring vocal hook
Ascending power-chord tension leading into Kim Thayil's microtonal wah-wah solo

harmonicFunction: Em (i) - Heavy, somber tonic anchor rumbling on the open low E string
G (♭III) - Blues-rock minor third lift providing forward motion
C (♭VI) - Dark submediant chord completing the natural minor cadence
A (IV) - Major IV chord injecting bright Dorian color in the chorus

techniques.name: 6/4 Time Signature Groove & Sludgy Palm Mutes
techniques.description: Internalizing the 6-beat measure (subdivided as 4/4 followed by a 2/4 measure) while playing heavy, sludgy low E palm-muted riffing

notes: Main riff on low E: Open E → fret 3 (G) → fret 2 (F#) → fret 3 on A string (C) → fret 2 on A (B)
Counting: 1-2-3-4 (riff) then 1-2 (chord stab) = 6 beats per measure
Chorus open chords: Em, G, C, and A
sequence: Play the low E single-note motif on beats 1 through 4
Stab the chord on beats 5 and 6
Maintain tight palm muting for punchy low-end definition
tips: Kim Thayil and Chris Cornell both played in standard tuning for this track, unlike many other Drop D Soundgarden songs
Lock into Matt Cameron's snare drum to keep the 6/4 pulse natural and swaying
Don't rush the extra two beats in the 6/4 measure—let the groove breathe

sections.name: 6/4 Metric Main Riff
sections.description: The brooding 6/4 riff that defines the song's hypnotic, off-kilter swing.
notes: Tight palm muting on the low E string notes
Clean chord stab on beat 5 and 6

sections.name: Chorus Explosion
sections.description: Full wall-of-sound chorus 'Just like every day, fell on black days'.
notes: Notice the uplifting major A chord at the end of the phrase
Lock tight with the drum cymbals

effects.distortion: Amp high-gain tube distortion boosted by subtle overdrive
effects.wah: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah (used for microtonal solo sweeps)

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Strumming
steps: Learn the four chorus chords: Em, G, C, and A
Recognize the major A chord that gives the chorus its Dorian color

intermediate.title: The 6/4 Metric Riff
steps: Internalize the 6-beat count: 4 beats of single notes + 2 beats of chord stabs
Coordinate the low E string walkdown with tight palm muting
Play along seamlessly with Matt Cameron's drum groove at 104 BPM

advanced.title: Full Arrangement & Kim Thayil Solo
steps: Learn Kim Thayil's microtonal wah solo and dissonant chord accents
Maintain relentless metric pocket across all dynamic changes
Capture the authentic Superunknown wall of sound live

commonMistakes: Trying to count the riff in 4/4 and dropping the last two beats of each bar
Playing G minor instead of G major in the chorus
Rushing the relaxed, heavy 104 BPM tempo
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: 6/4 counting drill out loud with metronome
5 minutes: Main riff low E single-note walkdown at 85 BPM → 104 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus open chord dynamic strumming
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 6/4 at 90 BPM, counting 1-2-3-4-5-6 with an accent on beat 1
